tasks.short: Instruct and drill personnel in assigned duties.

steps.what: Read the posted drill line for this session.
Instruct and drill fire department personnel in assigned duties, including firefighting, medical care, hazardous materials response and fire prevention.

tasks.design: The fire supervisor still instructs and drills fire department personnel in assigned duties, including firefighting, medical care, hazardous materials response and fire prevention. A drill line is already posted in the {DOCS}, with duty name, subject, session date, place and the author's name, so the hunt for that sheet is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The drill line sat on a paper sheet, so the supervisor hunted it before the session.
tasks.enabler_now: The training file already holds a drill line. Showing duty name, subject, session date, place and the author's name is configuration of that file.
tasks.still_hard: How to drill the crew in the room is the instruction. A posted line does not run the drill.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor sees the crew and refuses a line that does not name this session.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the drill. Less time goes to hunting a sheet. The supervisor still runs it.

reach.task: Post the drill line before the session.
reach.learn: The line needs duty name, subject, session date, place and the author's name, or the supervisor reads the paper sheet.

reach.task: Take part in the drill under this supervisor.
reach.learn: The drill is the supervisor's own instruction in the room. It is not a send, and the firefighter does not file a score.

reach.task: Leave hazardous-materials content with this supervisor for the drill.
reach.learn: The supervisor still teaches the response. A posted subject is not a completed drill.

evidence.claim: Instructing and drilling the crew stays with the fire supervisor. A posted drill line can be a shorter read. The drill itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.
Emotion recognition at work is prohibited. This design does not infer emotion from the crew or from the supervisor during the drill.
A data-protection assessment is mandatory for systematic employee monitoring and for body-worn cameras. This design does not monitor the crew and does not add a camera.
Staff monitoring needs works council consent. This design does not monitor the crew. The drill itself is unchanged.

The posted line is a duty name, a subject, a session date, a place and an author's name. It is not a competence score and not a camera clip. National rules vary. The digest names the Netherlands for the works-council and data-protection laws.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is only instructing and drilling fire department personnel in assigned duties, including firefighting, medical care, hazardous materials response, fire prevention and related subjects. Hiring, sizing up a fire and judging spend sit outside it. The training officer posts the line before the session.

Structured input: one drill line in the {DOCS} with duty name, subject, session date, place and the author's name. The line is the session subject, not a competence score and not a camera clip. If the line is missing or free text, the supervisor reads the paper sheet and that read is not shorter.

The supervisor still instructs and drills the crew in the room. Nothing is recorded by a machine, sent, or committed. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. Filing a drill record, a competence score, or sending a certificate outside the organisation would be its own step, with a gate on the final version. That step is not in this design, and it is not folded into the drill. The prior that the drill is a draft for someone else, or a send outside the organisation, is refused: it is the supervisor's own instruction in the room, and it is a write inside the organisation.

A model is not used. Existing system runtime is not the supervisor's time. The design does not score the crew, infer emotion, add a camera, monitor staff, or file a note. The in-person drill stays at full time.
unknowns: Whether this training file already has duty name, subject, session date, place and a name, or only a paper sheet.
Whether the site later wants a competence score filed. This design does not file one.
research_questions: Who posts the drill line, the training officer or the supervisor?
What share of sessions start with no line the supervisor can read?

already_counted.description: Reading a missing or free-text drill sheet by hand, inside the remaining read.

incremental.description: Checking that the drill line still names this session, duty, subject, session date, place and an author.

High: most lines carry the named fields and an author's name, and only that hunt shrinks. The drill stays. The high stays under the net after the field check.

tasks.short: Assess the fire and determine crew requirements.

steps.what: Read the posted building line before this incident.
Assess nature and extent of the fire, condition of the building, danger to adjacent buildings and water supply status, and determine crew or company requirements.

tasks.design: The fire supervisor still assesses the fire, the building, the danger to adjacent buildings and the water supply, and determines crew or company requirements on scene. A building line is already posted in the {DOCS}, with address, building use, water point, hazard note and the author's name, so the hunt for that card is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.

reach.task: Take the crew order from this supervisor on scene.
reach.learn: The spoken order is not a filed report, and the firefighter does not size up in the supervisor's place.

reach.task: Leave incident practice with this supervisor.
reach.learn: A drill card is not this incident. The supervisor still assesses the fire.

evidence.claim: Assessing the fire and determining crew or company requirements stays with the fire supervisor on scene. A posted building line can be a shorter read. The size-up itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.
